headline: Traders on the Kalshi prediction market now put the odds of a Tesla and SpaceX merger by 1 March 2027 at about 50%, after Elon Musk unveiled a new Tesla Roadster that uses SpaceX technology.
score_reason: Widely discussed speculation about a very large merger, backed only by betting odds and an analyst's view, with no statement from either company.
importance_line: A merger of the two companies, which together are worth more than $3 trillion, would affect the shareholders of both and Elon Musk's wider business empire, but the 50% figure is a betting market's view, neither company has commented, and Barclays notes a deal would need shareholder votes.
summary: The New York Post reports that Kalshi, a site where people bet on real-world events, gives about 50% odds that Tesla and SpaceX will merge by 1 March 2027, nearly 60% by 1 April and nearly 80% by the end of 2027, while CNBC's headline puts the odds above 50% for early 2027. Barclays analysts, quoted by Bloomberg, say a merger "has increasingly become the consensus expectation" and could come before Tesla's annual shareholder meeting, due by 6 December; neither company responded to requests for comment.
notes: CNBC original blocked; read the New York Post instead, which carries the Kalshi odds and relays Bloomberg's report on Barclays. CNBC is mentioned from its headline only.
